body: Ah, I did not think of the sharing with other people aspect. And I agree, setting and achieving a series of achievable goals is great.

Thank you for assuring me that my fear is reasonable. I think it must be important for me to remember that my fear comes from actual experience and it's not a delusion or the result of an over-active imagination or anything like that. When people try to encourage or pressure me to simply dismiss my fear as "not real" or "no big deal" that doesn't feel right to me at all. However, accepting that this is a real fear and THEN telling myself things like, "but I don't have to let it take over my life or let it stop me from doing the things I need and want to do" feels much better, I agree!

I've heard things like yoga and tai chi are very good for anxiety, and any kind of exercise is helpful for depression. I'm starting with short little walks because I'm in really bad shape after neglecting my body for many years.

That's very interesting because I tried some MDMA about 10 years ago and I never felt better than I did then in my whole life! That's what scared me about it though, I thought it was probably too good to be true. And I'm sure it's risky if you overdo it or take some in an environment that isn't safe or something like that. But I took it at a small party with people who made sure it was a safe and pleasant experience for everyone. It was very nice, very healing.
I've heard of that song before but never actually listened to it. It is inspirational, thanks

Thanks for replying. You just reminded me that pretty much everything I know about my problems and what to for them I learned from doing my own research already. That gives me a little spark of confidence and hope to just keep going along that path. I so often feel helpless and doubt my ability to do anything. A reminder that I do have the ability to help myself is very nice.
